## The Digital Marketplace Platform

The G-Cloud consists of a series of framework agreements with suppliers, from which public sector organisations can buy services without needing to run a full tender or their own competitive procurement process, and an online store – the Public Procurement Gateway, previously the Digital Marketplace, which allows public sector bodies to search for services that are covered by the G-Cloud frameworks.(no content)The Digital Marketplace was replaced by the Public Procurement Gateway in G-Cloud 13.

## Eligibility

All UK government departments, devolved administrations, local authorities, wider public-sector bodies, and arm's-length bodies can buy services in the marketplace.

## Overview

Greece's government procurement market is worth approximately €30 billion annually, and the system is undergoing significant modernization.

## Key Platform and Framework

The 2021 modernization law streamlined procedures, and the "promitheus.gov.gr" platform now hosts most tenders.(no content)The "Promitheus" platform is an independent electronic platform controlled by the Greek State and accessible world-wide for e-procurement awards.

## Legal Framework

The legal framework for public procurement is determined by law 4412/2016 "Public Works, Procurement and Services (Adaptation to EU Directives 2014/24 and 2014/25)", amended in 2021 and 2022, and law 4413/2016, which harmonize mandatory procedures for scheduling, overseeing, and awarding public procurement contracts, supplies, services and works contracts.

## Procurement Process

Procurement actions follow three stages: identification of agency needs and drafting the procurement program; publicizing the tender, selecting the best offer and awarding the contract; and implementation of the contract.

## Challenges

Despite progress, challenges remain, including bureaucracy and a focus on lowest price over quality.

Multiple specialized tender databases and platforms are available for those seeking to bid on Greek government ministry tenders.

As a member of the EU, the Czech Republic is subject to WTO Agreement on Government Procurement rules. ## Supervision

The administration of public tenders is closely watched in the Czech Republic, and the Office's objective is to achieve free and open competition between suppliers, along with selection of the best proposal in a transparent manner devoid of discrimination.
